rulings.evidence: Light cream cheese IS the 1/3-less-fat tub, so the vocabulary row 1/3 Fat Cream Cheese [1-3-fat-cream-cheese] is the same product and the form flag is a wording artefact. Preferred over the board's generic cream-cheese, which prices the full-fat brick at different macros.

Reduced-fat (2% milk) cheddar is the same product concept on the same shelf at the same per-ounce price class as block cheddar, so bid reuse is sound; the macro difference is carried by the label row returned here rather than by a bridged id. Not the shredded id - the source names cheese, not a bag, and the instructions grate it.
The source itself glosses semi-skimmed as 2% milk, which is the same-form vocabulary row Milk [milk] and the board's 7 of 7 match; a reuse, not a form flip.

Measured by the teaspoon inside a spice list and blended into a sauce, which is the dried spice-jar flake, not a fresh bunch - fresh parsley at 1 tsp is not a purchasable measure and is a different price and gram weight. Board carries no commodity for it, so the term goes to pricing.
1 tsp squeezed into a blended cheese sauce is the prepared condiment, not dry powder; exact same-form vocabulary row Yellow Mustard [mustard], board 7 of 7 at 0.0495.

'Reduced' is an incomplete label word (the source is a UK macro site, so most likely reduced-sugar) and no such product concept exists as a separate id; the purchased bottle is BBQ sauce, vocabulary row BBQ Sauce [bbq-sauce], board 7 of 7. Macros use a standard sauce label, which is the conservative direction.

'Low calorie' describes the spray delivery, not a different food - every aerosol cooking spray is oil per spray; board cooking-spray at 7 of 7, a reuse. Unquantified by the source, so weighed at about ten 1-second sprays (3 g at source scale) rather than left at zero.

Rename of the bare intake term onto the vocabulary's generic dry-pasta row Ziti Pasta [pasta] (same form, board 7 of 7); shape is not a food identity or price difference for dry short pasta. Buy string names macaroni because the dish is mac and cheese.

macro_cross_check: Source publishes 642 cal / 75.3 carbs / 58.5 protein per serving over 4 servings. Recomputed at source scale over all 22 lines: about 3070 cal, 202.6 g protein, 323 g carbs total = 767 cal / 50.7 P / 80.7 C per serving. Protein is 13.4% under the source's figure - inside the 15% bar but the widest gap in this batch, and it is a PRODUCT difference, not a portion one: the main protein is stated by the source in grams (400 g diced breast = 100 g raw per serving, no each-weight assumption available to get wrong), and the shortfall sits in the two cheeses, where US 1/3-less-fat cream cheese carries 2 g protein per 28 g against a UK light cream cheese's roughly 3 g, and Kraft 2% cheddar is leaner in protein per 100 g than a UK 30%-reduced-fat block. The same substitution explains calories running 19.5% high (US 1/3-less-fat cream cheese is about 250 cal/100 g against UK Philadelphia Light at about 165). Carbs agree at +7%. In band: 767 cal (450-800, though close to the ceiling) and 50.7 g protein (>= 40).
